# The Bench Caelestinus Central answers to no navy. Since the Caelestinus Accord, neither does the law.
## The Accord When [textlink="Kyphrus" link="WFLoreCollapse"] fell and [textlink="the Lattice" link="WFLoreLattice"] woke, the TSF and the Vanguard each knew one thing for certain: the other could not be allowed to hold the anchors. Nobody in Colossus can call for help from outside, so there was nobody to ask. They signed the Caelestinus Accord instead. It gives the anchors, and the station at their centre, to a third party sworn to neither.
That party is the Bench. It holds the [textlink="Common Writ" link="WFCommonWrit"], the sector's law, and both navies put up with judges boarding their ships because the alternative is the other navy doing it.
## The Overseer The Overseer presides over the Bench. They open and close worlds to landing, post standing ordinances, issue the Deep Writs that let a ship past the anchors, and pardon. Only the Overseer may raise a relay anchor and push lawful space outward.
## The judges Judges are the Bench's officers. Most were Federation contractors once, and came to Caelestinus when they saw how the war was fought. They are sworn to the Writ, not paid by the station, and they are impossible to bribe.
- A judge hails before they shoot. - A judge writes a ticket before they arrest. - A judge outlaws before they kill.
Most captains never hear from a judge. The ones carrying things from beyond the anchors do.
## The fleet - The [bold]Lightning[/bold], an interceptor, carries an ion disruptor that stalls a ship which will not heave to. - The [bold]Roswell[/bold], an arrestor, carries a tractor beam and a WRIT disabler harpoon that cuts a ship's jump drive and holds it fast. - The [bold]Hornet[/bold] patrols with non-lethal guns, and the [bold]Petra[/bold] stands up to anything larger until help comes.
Two judge ships fly a standing patrol around Caelestinus Central, and a lost ship is replaced within the hour.
## In bond What the Bench seizes goes into bond. Nobody outside the Bench sees where. Judges who serve long enough notice that the bonded vault never seems to fill.
## From the record Ticket stub, found in the pocket of a dead Reaver, Slack band.
"Bench of Caelestinus. Ticket number withheld. Charge: Trespass beyond the Anchors. Fine: 10,000. Taken: 0. Owed: 10,000."
Written on the back, in a different hand: "Still owed."
